title: Docker images that never download at run time
description: Fetch weights and kernel binaries while the image is built, then forbid every download at run time with FASTFORKS_OFFLINE=1 (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is honoured too). A file that is…
html:
Fetch weights and kernel binaries while the image is built, then forbid every download at run time with FASTFORKS_OFFLINE=1 (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is honoured too). A file that is not in the image then raises an error naming the file and the fastforks download command that fetches it, instead of reaching for the network.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM python:3.12-slim AS build
ENV FASTFORKS_CACHE=/opt/fastforks-cache VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH
RUN python -m venv $VIRTUAL_ENV
# torch is a dependency of fastforks; for a specific CUDA build add e.g. --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130
# (it must match the kernels, see `fastforks env`). For a lean or commercial image install fastforks-core with the extras
# the models you ship need, e.g. "fastforks-core[timm]" (see the README).
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install fastforks
# explicit model list; --arch = the GPUs this image runs on (no GPU needed to build). Drop --kernels for CPU-only.
# HF_TOKEN (gated or private repos) only as a BuildKit secret: never ENV / ARG, it would stay in a layer.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=hf_token \
    HF_TOKEN="$(cat /run/secrets/hf_token 2>/dev/null)" \
    fastforks download hitnet-eth3d igev-stereo-sceneflow --kernels --arch sm_86,sm_89 --commercial-only \
 && fastforks download hitnet-eth3d igev-stereo-sceneflow --kernels --arch sm_86,sm_89 --check \
 && chmod -R a+rX /opt/fastforks-cache

FROM python:3.12-slim
COPY --from=build /opt/venv /opt/venv
COPY --from=build /opt/fastforks-cache /opt/fastforks-cache
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH FASTFORKS_CACHE=/opt/fastforks-cache FASTFORKS_OFFLINE=1 \
    TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/triton TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/inductor
USER 1000

Gated weights land in the Hugging Face cache, so copy HF_HOME (or HF_HUB_CACHE) too, or put the file on FASTFORKS_WEIGHTS_PATH.

Build with docker build --secret id=hf_token,env=HF_TOKEN . (or leave the secret out); run with docker run --gpus all --read-only --tmpfs /tmp IMAGE .... Without --gpus the image runs the portable CPU path.

  • download ... --check as a last RUN fails the build (exit 1, MISSING ... on stderr) if a file cannot be resolved without network, so a broken image is found at build time, not at the first request. It never touches the network and prints where each file resolves from. "Resolvable" includes FASTFORKS_WEIGHTS_PATH / FASTFORKS_KERNEL_PATH and the Hugging Face / torch hub caches; in a clean build stage those are empty, so every hit is in FASTFORKS_CACHE. --dry-run lists the size and licence class per model first and fetches nothing.
  • GPU -> --arch: RTX 30xx sm_86, A100 sm_80, RTX 40xx / L4 sm_89, H100 sm_90, B200 sm_100, RTX 50xx sm_120 (all in Other GPUs); several: --arch sm_89,sm_120.
  • --arch takes sm_89, 8.9 or native, validated against the kernel manifest and resolved as at run time (an sm_86 GPU gets the binary the runtime would pick). --arch needs --kernels and excludes --all-archs; targets like sm_90a are not offered (use sm_90); an all-archs set is needlessly large for an image.
  • --kernels-only fetches the kernel binaries without weights (all libraries, or those of the named models); --arch / --all-archs / --check work as with --kernels.
  • The cache is a plain directory; treat it as opaque, copy it whole, and use the same fastforks major version to read it. fastforks creates cache directories private (0700), so the build stage ends with chmod -R a+rX (above) or the non-root user cannot read them. A read-only cache then works: files are only read, a failed write of the verification stamp is ignored. Inside a container download refuses to run while FASTFORKS_OFFLINE is set (unset it for that step).
  • Instead of baking, mount a pre-filled cache as a read-only volume (-v cache:/opt/fastforks-cache:ro), or point FASTFORKS_WEIGHTS_PATH / FASTFORKS_KERNEL_PATH at read-only directories of the original files.
  • JIT caches are written at run time (Triton, torch.compile): point TRITON_CACHE_DIR and TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR at a writable directory (--tmpfs), or the first call is slow and a read-only filesystem fails. torch.compile also needs a C++ compiler in the image.
  • A nvidia/cuda:*-runtime base needs a host driver that is new enough for the kernels' CUDA version; fastforks env prints what the kernels need.

Licences

Baking weights into an image that you push to a registry is redistribution. fastforks download without a model list fetches every installed model, including non-commercial and GPL families, and warns about it. Build the image from your own explicit model list, use --commercial-only to skip models not cleared for commercial use (with a model list it fails if you name one that is not cleared), and do not push images holding non-commercial weights to public registries. fastforks info MODEL shows the terms.

Offline installs (wheelhouse)

On a machine with network: pip download fastforks torch -d wheelhouse (add --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 for a CUDA build of torch that matches the kernels), then copy wheelhouse/ and the cache (fastforks download ...). On the air-gapped machine: pip install --no-index --find-links wheelhouse fastforks.
